hook.line: Some news is a surprise to nobody. Hernando has watched the block change for years, and he always says the same thing: sooner or later, it all comes out.
hook.es: Tarde o temprano se va a enterar.
hook.en: Sooner or later he's going to find out.

rule:
For something that could not have been avoided, say *era inevitable* (it was) or *es inevitable* (it is). *Inevitable* is the same for *el* and *la* words; only the plural adds *-s*: *cambios inevitables*.

To say what is inevitable, add *que* and the subjunctive: *Es inevitable que haya retrasos*. You met this with *es importante que*: the same family of opinion phrases.

Two more ways to say it. *Inevitablemente* works like an adverb: *Inevitablemente, los precios van a subir*. *Tarde o temprano* says it will happen in the end, whenever.
smallPrint: Teachers call these impersonal expressions. After them, a *que* clause takes the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *Era* or *Es*: ___ inevitable. (It was inevitable.) Type the whole sentence.
Choose *haya* or *hay*: Es inevitable que ___ retrasos. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: After *es inevitable que*, use the subjunctive: *haya*.

yourTurn.prompt: Sooner or later he's going to find out.
yourTurn.answer: Tarde o temprano se va a enterar.
yourTurn.why: *Tarde o temprano* is a fixed phrase for "in the end".

yourTurn.prompt: Inevitably, prices are going to go up.
yourTurn.answer: Inevitablemente, los precios van a subir.

yourTurn.prompt: It's inevitable that there will be protests.
yourTurn.why: The same pattern: *es inevitable que* plus *haya*.
Switch *es* to *era* (or *fue* for a single moment).

yourTurn.prompt: Sooner or later everyone is going to know the truth.
yourTurn.answer: Tarde o temprano todos van a saber la verdad.
accept: Tarde o temprano todos van a conocer la verdad.
yourTurn.why: Same fixed phrase, then a normal sentence.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *es inevitable que*, Spanish uses the subjunctive: *haya*.

pitfalls.wrong: Inevitable, los precios van a subir.
pitfalls.right: Inevitablemente, los precios van a subir.
pitfalls.why: For "inevitably" you need the adverb ending in *-mente*.

pitfalls.wrong: Es inevitable para los precios subir.
pitfalls.right: Es inevitable que los precios suban.
pitfalls.why: English says *for prices to go up*; Spanish says *que* plus the subjunctive.

personal: Think of something small and boring that is inevitable in your life. Say it with *tarde o temprano* or *es inevitable que*.
